3.6 Futhermore, Victory Fire agrees with Prof. Asif Sohail Usmani and Prof. Jiang Liming’s recommendations in relation to additional FSI protection for renovation works [ER3/2254/§7.3.1(g)]:

“Caution against the occupation of removed buildings and supply additional FSI protection: Residents may be cautioned against occupying high-rise buildings under maintenance and renovation, and the regulatory bar should be raised where this is considered unavoidable by providing for top-up safety protection to the occupants during the event of a fire. This may require installing redundant FSI systems before the commencement of the building maintenance and renovation work as part of temporary works undertaken. The requirement of redundant safety measures must be implemented on top of the normal fire safety work, with additional measures mandated for longer duration projects lasting longer than an acceptable duration. For projects exceeding that call for the most vulnerable occupants (based on utility and the height of the floor they occupy and distance from the exits) should be considered.”

3.7 Victory Fire also agrees with FSD that new technology shall be introduced.

Mr. Kenny in his 1st witness statement proposes new technology based temporary measures to give alert to occupants in the event that FAS was out of service [WS1/43/11.4]:

“Finally, in situations involving the failure of a FAS, it is recommended that property owners, management bodies, and the RFSIC take proactive steps to promptly and effectively notify building occupants of a shutdown of the property’s FSI system, both through the FAS such notification should include posting detailed information about the shutdown at the entrances, inside the main lobby, outside the F.S. control room and a prominent location that can attract the attention of building occupants, such as mailboxes, operable component, and distributing notices to each occupant’s mailbox. To ensure that all residents are adequately informed. In the long term, the FSD will explore more reliable, practical, and technology-based temporary measures to provide real-time alerts in the event of a fire when the alarm system is temporarily out of service.”
